# Volatility-timing backtest — economic-significance findings

*Generated by `vol_timing_backtest.py` (`cli.py run economics`) on real S&P-500 (.SPX) returns +
RV forecasts, same rows/splits as the statistical study. Converts each model's one-step RV
forecast into a Fleming–Kirby–Ostdiek (2001) volatility-timing strategy: scale exposure inversely
to forecast variance to hold risk at a 10% annualized target; 1 bp/turnover cost; 3× leverage cap.*

## Strategy
`w_t = (target_daily_vol) / sqrt(RV_forecast_t)`, clipped to [0, 3]; strategy return
`w_t · r_t − cost·|Δw_t|`. The RV forecast of day *t* uses only ≤ t−1 information (leakage-free),
so sizing day-*t* exposure with it is causal. We compare buy & hold vs timing on HAR, HAR-X and
CHIMERA forecasts, and the annual certainty-equivalent (CE) fee a γ=2 mean–variance investor would
pay to switch.

## Results

**Calm window (test ≈ 2014–2020, 1509 days):**

| strategy | Ann.Ret | Ann.Vol | Sharpe | net Sharpe | max DD | turnover |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy & Hold     | 0.099 | 0.130 | 0.76 | 0.76 | −0.20 | 0.0 |
| HAR-timed      | 0.102 | 0.131 | **0.80** | **0.78** | −0.20 | 33.6 |
| HAR-X-timed    | 0.098 | 0.132 | 0.77 | 0.74 | −0.21 | 34.2 |
| CHIMERA-timed  | 0.092 | 0.127 | 0.76 | 0.72 | −0.20 | 39.8 |

CE fee: HAR→HAR-X **−43 bp/yr**, HAR-X→CHIMERA **−46 bp/yr**.

**Crisis window (train < 2007; GFC 2008–09 in test, 1510 days):**

| strategy | Ann.Ret | Ann.Vol | Sharpe | net Sharpe | max DD | turnover |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Buy & Hold     | 0.001 | 0.245 | 0.00 | 0.00 | **−0.61** | 0.0 |
| HAR-timed      | 0.016 | 0.124 | **0.14** | **0.13** | **−0.32** | 15.9 |
| HAR-X-timed    | 0.002 | 0.124 | 0.03 | 0.02 | −0.36 | 20.4 |
| CHIMERA-timed  | −0.000| 0.126 | 0.02 | −0.00 | −0.36 | 21.9 |

CE fee: HAR→HAR-X **−140 bp/yr**, HAR-X→CHIMERA **−25 bp/yr**.

## Verdict (economic)

1. **Volatility timing is genuinely valuable for risk management.** In the GFC crisis it nearly
   **halves the max drawdown (−61% → −32%)** and turns a 0.00 Sharpe into 0.14, while holding
   realized vol at target — a concrete, deployable benefit for a desk (hedging / dynamic risk
   limits). This is the honest *positive* business takeaway.
2. **No economic quantum advantage, and not even a feature advantage here.** The **simplest HAR**
   forecast captures essentially all of the timing benefit; HAR-X and CHIMERA produce *negative*
   CE fees (an investor would pay NOT to switch), because their marginally different forecasts add
   turnover/noise without improving risk-adjusted return. So the quantum reservoir adds **nothing
   a desk can monetize** beyond a plain HAR vol-timer — fully consistent with the statistical
   negative (RMSE/QLIKE) and the cross-asset/COVID results.

This replaces a generic "$30B TAM" impact claim with a concrete, honest economic statement:
*the deployable lever is volatility timing on a simple realized-variance forecast; the quantum
reservoir does not improve the dollar outcome at simulable scale.*
